project.name: my-forever-music
project.description: Platform-independent music curation & recommendation system: a Spring Boot Java API, a React/TypeScript web app, and a FastAPI Python AI service that build a user-owned playlist/taste library (PMS) and an editorial discovery + recommendation loop (EMS/GMS).

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Defines the cached application Settings (LLM endpoint, model names, artifact directory) loaded from environment variables for the FastAPI AI service.
nodes.languageNotes: Cached get_settings() returns a Settings object populated from os.getenv.

nodes.summary: FastAPI application entry point that instantiates the app and registers all feature routers (health, recommendations, EMS, audio features, public curations, datasets).

nodes.languageNotes: torch.nn.Module with embeddings feeding a TransformerEncoder; mean-pools the masked sequence to score items.

nodes.name: SasrecMvpModel

nodes.name: sasrec_model_registry_service.py

nodes.summary: Manages SASRec model lifecycle in a JSON registry: latest-model resolution, promote/disable/rollback, and artifact metadata snapshots.

nodes.name: sasrec_offline_report_service.py
nodes.summary: Service computing leave-last-out offline evaluation metrics (hit-rate, MRR, NDCG) for a SASRec dataset using a heuristic candidate ranker.

nodes.summary: Produces SASRec offline reports: evaluates each example via recency-based ranking and aggregates ranking metrics at k.

nodes.name: sasrec_ranking_service.py
nodes.summary: Service loading a persisted SASRec model artifact and scoring candidate tracks, returning ranked candidates with normalized scores.

nodes.name: SasrecRankingService

nodes.name: sasrec_training_service.py
nodes.summary: Service running the full SASRec MVP training loop: dataset prep, PyTorch training, leave-last-out evaluation, metric/qualification gating, and artifact persistence.

nodes.name: SasrecTrainingService

nodes.name: centroid

layers.name: API Layer
layers.description: HTTP entry points: Spring @RestController classes in each module presentation package, FastAPI APIRouter modules in the AI service, exposing REST endpoints for auth, platform, pms, ems, gms, recommendation, melon and public-curation features

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.description: Core business logic and orchestration: Spring module application services, stores and schedulers, FastAPI service/job modules, and React hooks, contexts, API client and lib utilities that drive client-side stateful logic

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.description: Persistence and external-integration adapters: Spring module infrastructure (JPA persistence plus Spotify/Tidal/YouTube/Last.fm/Melon and AI adapters), Flyway SQL migrations and their tables, and AI service ORM/data models

layers.name: Types Layer
layers.description: Shared data contracts: Spring presentation Request/Response DTOs, FastAPI Pydantic request/response schemas, and React TypeScript type definitions used across the music-curation domain

layers.name: UI Layer
layers.description: React presentation: route-level pages, reusable components (visualizer, home, layout), layouts, the App/main bootstrap and static assets/styles for the my-forever-music web client

layers.name: Test Layer
layers.description: Automated verification: Spring unit and WebMvc controller tests, FastAPI pytest suites, and the apps/web regression and product-flow harness scripts

layers.name: Configuration Layer
layers.description: Build and runtime configuration: Gradle/Vite/TypeScript build files, application*.yml profiles, the Spring Boot and FastAPI entry points, shared common error handling, and repo tooling settings

layers.name: Infrastructure Layer
layers.description: Deployment and environment setup: docker-compose stacks, nginx HTTPS configs, systemd units and Ubuntu/MacBook provisioning scripts under infra/

layers.name: Documentation Layer
layers.description: Project documentation: architecture, design and guide markdown under docs/ plus root README, AGENTS and CLAUDE guidance files

layers.name: Scratch & Scaffolding
layers.description: Non-production artifacts: brainstorm HTML mockups, codex backups, runtime data state, desktop/packages workspace placeholders and other scaffolding stubs

tour.title: What Is My Forever Music
tour.description: Start here. The README defines my-forever-music as a service that imports playlists from streaming platforms and preserves them as a user-owned music taste library that survives switching providers. It introduces the three core domains the whole codebase is organized around: PMS (the user's personal music space), EMS (an external-exploration space that collects public playlists and trends), and GMS (a gateway space holding recommendations that passed the user's taste model). Keep these three letters in mind, they recur throughout the tour.

tour.title: Architecture and Tech Stack
tour.description: Before reading code, understand the shape of the system. The PROJECT_GUIDE is the primary onboarding document, and TECH_STACK explains the polyglot split: a React + TypeScript + Vite web app, a Spring Boot 3.5 / Java 21 main API, and a FastAPI / Python 3.12 AI service, backed by PostgreSQL and Redis. These docs justify why recommendation logic is split between a Java orchestrator and a Python brain, which the later steps make concrete.

tour.title: Spring API Bootstrap and Config
tour.description: This is the heart of the backend. MyForeverMusicApiApplication is the Spring Boot entry point that boots the main API, and application.yml binds the datasource, JPA/Flyway, actuator, and the extensive app.* properties that tune EMS discovery, schedulers, and platform OAuth. Spring component-scans the modules/* packages from here, so every service, controller, and adapter you meet later is wired up at this single starting point.
tour.languageLesson: Spring Boot uses @SpringBootApplication on the main class to enable auto-configuration and component scanning of the surrounding package tree. Profile-specific YAML files (application-local.yml, application-database.yml, application-prod.yml) override the base application.yml depending on the active SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE.

tour.title: Auth: The User Foundation
tour.description: Everything personal in the system hangs off a user account, so auth is the foundational module. AuthAccountStore is a repository-style interface abstracting account persistence (registration, lookup by id/email, Last.fm profile linkage), and it ranks near the top of the codebase by fan-in because so many features depend on knowing who the user is. The interface has both an in-memory implementation for local boot and a JPA implementation backed by the auth_user_account table you will see in the schema step.
tour.languageLesson: This project follows a hexagonal / ports-and-adapters layout per module: an application package holds business logic and store interfaces (ports), while infrastructure/local and infrastructure/persistence packages hold the adapters (in-memory vs JPA). This is why nearly every store has two implementations.

tour.title: Platform Provider Abstraction
tour.description: To import playlists from many streaming services without scattering vendor logic, the platform module defines PlatformPlaylistProvider, a strategy interface for listing and importing playlists from an external platform. The Spotify and TIDAL adapters implement it, each fetching the user's playlists and enriching tracks with audio features via the ReccoBeats client. Building on the User foundation from Step 4, a connected platform credential lets these providers act on the user's behalf.
tour.languageLesson: Java interface + multiple @Component implementations selected at runtime is the classic Strategy pattern. A registry bean typically resolves the right provider by platform id, keeping callers like the PMS importer ignorant of vendor-specific OAuth and API quirks.

tour.title: PMS: Importing the Taste Library
tour.description: Now the PMS domain comes alive. PmsPlaylistImportService orchestrates the core user journey: it bootstraps an import workspace, refreshes platform credentials, fetches playlists through the providers from Step 5, and persists them into the user's library. This is the moment a user's external playlists become owned, durable data — exactly the product promise from Step 1's README.

tour.title: EMS: Editorial Signal Acquisition
tour.description: While PMS captures what the user already likes, EMS explores what is new. EmsAcquisitionService runs the editorial acquisition pipeline: it fetches articles from RSS sources (Pitchfork, Stereogum, NME, and more), extracts musical signals via the AI service, turns them into Spotify/TIDAL seeds, and persists runs, signals, and seeds for the discovery pool. This pipeline is what keeps the recommendation candidate pool fresh and grounded in real-world music journalism.

tour.title: The AI Service Entry Point
tour.description: Switch languages and services. main.py is the FastAPI entry point for the Python AI service; it instantiates the app and registers every feature router (health, recommendations, EMS, audio-feature inference, public curations, datasets). This is the Python counterpart to the Spring bootstrap in Step 3 — the second runtime that the Java API calls over HTTP for the intelligence-heavy work.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI composes an application from APIRouter modules via app.include_router(...). Each router declares path operations with type-annotated request/response Pydantic schemas, giving automatic validation and OpenAPI docs for free.

tour.title: The Recommendation Brain: SASRec
tour.description: Here is what makes the AI service worth a separate runtime. recommendation_service.py produces a deterministic recommendation preview by resolving a seed strategy and synthesizing ranked, explained items, while sasrec_training_service.py runs the full SASRec training loop (dataset prep, PyTorch training, leave-last-out evaluation, and metric gating). The underlying sasrec.py model is a Transformer encoder over the track vocabulary that predicts the next item a user would want — the learned personalization signal the rest of the system feeds on.
tour.languageLesson: SASRec (Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation) treats a user's listening history as a sequence and uses a Transformer's self-attention to weight which past tracks matter for the next prediction. Item and position embeddings feed the encoder, whose final logits rank the entire track vocabulary.

tour.title: GMS: Closing the Recommendation Loop
tour.description: GMS is the gateway where PMS taste, EMS candidates, and the AI brain converge. GmsRecommendationPreviewService fetches previews from the AI service via AiRecommendationPreviewClient, then reranks them with SASRec, audio-taste, and taste-mode signals and computes six evidence axes (affinity, novelty, coherence, diversity, redundancy, confidence). The RECOMMENDATION_LOOP_POLICY document sets the principles behind this feedback loop, where user reactions flow back to refine PMS — the core engine implied by Steps 6, 7, and 9.

tour.title: The Web Front End
tour.description: Now the user-facing layer. main.tsx mounts the React root inside auth, playback, and recommendation-workspace context providers, and App.tsx defines the routing tree that wires every page to the shared layout. AuthSessionContext and PlaybackContext are high-fan-in providers: the former manages the logged-in session (mirroring Step 4's accounts), while the latter orchestrates a unified queue across Spotify, TIDAL, and YouTube playback engines.
tour.languageLesson: React Context lets a provider expose state to any descendant via a custom hook (useAuthSession, usePlayback) without prop-drilling. Wrapping App in nested providers in main.tsx makes session and playback state ambient across the entire routing tree.

tour.title: The Browser-to-Backend Contract
tour.description: The front end talks to the Spring API through one disciplined seam. services/api.ts is the central browser API client, wrapping fetch with JSON and error handling and exposing 100+ typed functions covering auth, OAuth, PMS/EMS/GMS, and playback. types/api.ts is the shared barrel of request/response interfaces that mirror the Java DTOs — the single source of truth that keeps the TypeScript client and Java server in agreement.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript interfaces describe API shapes at compile time only — they erase at runtime, so the api.ts wrapper still validates and narrows responses. Centralizing every endpoint in one client plus one types barrel makes backend contract changes a single, traceable edit on the web side.

tour.title: The Database Schema
tour.description: Underneath all the services sits a Flyway-managed PostgreSQL schema, applied as ordered V##__ migrations. V4 creates auth_user_account (the accounts behind Step 4), V37 creates recommendation_audit_log that records each recommendation's model and dataset version plus fallback reasons (the audit trail for Step 10's loop), and V48 creates the public-curation storage for shareable AI-curated playlists. Reading the migrations top to bottom shows how the data model grew alongside the features.
tour.languageLesson: Flyway applies migration files in version order (V1, V2, ... V50) exactly once, tracking applied versions in a schema-history table. Migrations should be immutable once shipped and forward-only, so the schema evolves deterministically across every environment.

tour.title: Local Stack and Deployment
tour.description: Finally, how it all runs. The local Docker Compose stack provisions PostgreSQL 17 and Redis 7 with health checks and persistent volumes, bound to localhost, giving the Spring API a real database for the database profile from Step 3. vite.config.ts complements it on the web side, proxying /api calls to the backend during development so the front end and API behave as one origin. Together these close the loop from source code to a running, testable system on a developer's machine.
tour.languageLesson: docker-compose declares services with health checks and named volumes for persistence; binding ports to 127.0.0.1 keeps the dev database off the network. The Vite dev server's proxy config forwards matching request paths to the API, avoiding CORS during local development.
